Divergence distribution goodness-of-fit vs. the Gaussian identity-draw assumption

Ting-Hsuan Chen

02 November, 2026

  • 0. Setup directory
  • 1. Load real per-locus data for the five validation genomes
  • 2. Item 32: distribution fitting and goodness-of-fit
  • 3. Item 36: former identity_fix adjustment, before/after comparison
  • 4. Notes / caveats for the manuscript response

This script covers two closely related revision items that share the same input data (the five validation species’ real RepeatMasker per-locus records, processed_output.temp, already used for item 31):

  • Item 32 (R1#2, R1#7): fit skew-normal and gamma distributions, alongside the Gaussian currently assumed by modes 0/1/2’s identity draw, to the empirical per-family/per-genome divergence data, and report KS-statistic/AIC/BIC goodness-of-fit.
  • Item 36 (R2#3): before/after sensitivity check on the identity_fix ascertainment-bias adjustment (identity + (100 - identity) * 0.5) that TEgenomeSimulator <= v1.0.0 applied on top of the raw Gaussian draw in TE_sim_random_insertion.py’s generate_sequence() (and in TE_sim_nested_insertion.py) - show the identity distribution pre- and post-adjustment against the real empirical distribution. The adjustment has since been removed from the simulator (commit efa3369), partly on the basis of this comparison; the current simulator mutates each copy with the raw Gaussian draw directly, so section 3 documents the former behaviour.

Only the real (original) genome RepeatMasker data is used below - not mode-2 simulated output - because both items ask whether the simulator’s generative assumption (a Gaussian, and formerly the identity_fix transform) matches real biology, not whether the simulator reproduces its own input parameters.

How to run: sbatch --cpus-per-task=5 --mem=48G -t 1-00:00:00 -J gof_knit -o gof_knit.%j.out -e gof_knit.%j.err --wrap "cd /workspace/cflthc/script/TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/revision && Rscript -e \"rmarkdown::render('23.1_item32_divergence_gof.Rmd')\""

1. Load real per-locus data for the five validation genomes

2. Item 32: distribution fitting and goodness-of-fit

2.1 Family-level fitting (top 10 families per superfamily)

Per-family fits cover the 10 most abundant families (by copy number, N >= 30) of each superfamily that holds >= 1% of a genome’s loci. Class-only or unclassified labels (“DNA”, “LTR”, “Unknown”, “*/unknown”, “SINE?”) and non-TE repeats (satellites, simple repeats, rDNA, knobs, centromeric/subtelomeric repeats, endogenous viruses) are left out of the per-family fits but stay in the genome-pooled fit (section 2.2). Groups larger than 20,000 loci are fitted on a random sample of that size (fixed seed); n is the full number of loci and n_fit the number fitted.

Selecting the most abundant families favours families with many copies, which tend to have smoother, more regular divergence distributions than rare families. The coverage table below gives the share of each genome’s loci that the selected families represent, so the scope of the family-level results is explicit.

Reviewer 1 named maize Gypsy/Copia specifically - these are flagged separately in the summary table (superfamily matches “Gypsy”/“Copia”, case-insensitive) so they are easy to find without scanning the full table.

3. Item 36: former identity_fix adjustment, before/after comparison

identity_fix was applied by TEgenomeSimulator <= v1.0.0 and has since been removed (commit efa3369): the current simulator mutates each copy with the raw Gaussian draw (“raw draw” below), so “post-fix” is the former behaviour, kept here as the before/after evidence for R2#3.

For each genome (pooled) and the maize Gypsy/Copia families named by Reviewer 1, draw simulated identity values from rnorm(mean_identity_pct, sd_identity_pct) using that group’s own real mean/SD (the same statistic mode 2 would estimate), replicate get_identity()’s resample-if-over-100 and truncate-to-integer behaviour (the current simulator also resamples draws below 0, which never occur at these means/SDs), then apply the former identity_fix transform and compare all three curves (real / raw draw / post-fix) on the percent-divergence scale.

Mean/SD of real identity vs. simulated raw Gaussian draw (current simulator) vs. post-identity_fix draw (former adjustment, <= v1.0.0), and KS statistic of each simulated distribution against the real one. identity_fix is a fixed affine transform (y = 0.5x + 50), so it halves the SD and shifts the mean toward 100 without changing distribution shape - it does not address any tail-heaviness/skewness gap, it only narrows and relocates the (still-Gaussian) draw.

4. Notes / caveats for the manuscript response

  • The empirical divergence data used for both the GOF fitting (section 2) and the identity_fix comparison (section 3) is itself measured by RepeatMasker on the real genomes. RepeatMasker’s detection sensitivity is known to decline at high divergence, so this empirical distribution is likely right-censored - it probably under-represents the most divergent, hardest-to-detect relics. Any deviation from Gaussian reported here should therefore be read as a conservative (lower-bound) estimate of the true mismatch between the Gaussian assumption and real biology.
  • KS statistics in section 2 are reported without p-values, since gofstat()’s asymptotic KS null distribution assumes known (not MLE-fitted) parameters. AIC/BIC (which do not have this issue) are the primary basis for ranking the three candidate distributions; the KS statistic is reported as a descriptive effect-size alongside them.
  • identity_fix (item 36) was a deterministic affine transform of the raw Gaussian draw (y = 0.5x + 50), so it was analytically still Gaussian - it could not fix a shape mismatch (skewness/heavy tail) reported in section 2; it only shifted and narrowed the draw. Section 3’s summary table confirms this empirically (post-fix SD ~= 0.5 x raw-draw SD), and shows the post-fix draw sits much further from the real distribution than the raw draw. The adjustment was therefore removed from the simulator (commit efa3369, after v1.0.0); all revised simulations use the raw draw, and the identity in the output GFF is the identity used to mutate the copy.
  • Per-family fits cover only the 10 most abundant families of each retained superfamily (26-51% of each genome’s loci; see the coverage table in section 2.1). Abundant families tend to have smoother, more regular divergence distributions than rare ones, so the family-level results describe the families that dominate each genome rather than every family. The genome-pooled fits (section 2.2) use all loci.
  • Groups with more than 20,000 loci are fitted on a random sample of that size (fixed seed); at that sample size the AIC/BIC ranking and the KS statistic are stable, and the full n is reported alongside n_fit.
